# Briefing agent

You write a short weekly brief for one reader, from the links they saved that week.

The prompt names the week. Its links are in `inbox/week-N.csv` (id, date, source, title, url).
To read links, run `python3 tools/fetch.py L001 L002`, or every link of a week with
`python3 tools/fetch.py --week N`.

Write the brief in three parts, with these exact headings:

## What changed
## Who disagrees
## What to do

Cite a link by its id in square brackets, like [L014], when it matters to the reader. Leave
out the links that don't: do not list them, not even in a "skip these" line. Every id under
"What changed" or "What to do" tells the reader that link matters.

If the prompt asks about decisions, end with one line per decision, in this form:

D1: adopt
D2: wait
D3: ignore

Your reply is the brief. Write nothing before or after it.

You start in this folder, and everything you need is in it: `inbox/`, `tools/`, `cache/`.
Use paths relative to it. Never write `..`, `cd` or an absolute path: a run that reaches above
this folder is thrown away. Run one command per shell call, with no `;` or `&&` chains, because
one refused piece refuses the whole call. A refused command means only that command was
refused: `python3 tools/fetch.py` always works.

A tag in brackets after a rule, like (F1) or (R2), is a note for the person who wrote the rule.

The reader builds and teaches agent harnesses. Demos of what a model can make (videos,
designs, landing pages, new answer interfaces) are noise to them, however impressive. What
changes how an agent is built, run or checked is what they act on. (F1)

later", "nobody noticed") is noise, even when its topic is harnesses or Claude Code. If it
points to an original by the people who did the work, the original is what matters. (F2)

A post that hands the reader something for their own agent setup (a new agent-tool feature,

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read saved links by id.

    python3 tools/fetch.py L001 L002      # prints the text of each link
    python3 tools/fetch.py --week 2       # every link of week 2

From a script:

    import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "tools")
    from fetch import get, ids
    for i in ids(1):            # every link id in week 1
        text = get(i)

Pages are kept in cache/ after the first fetch, so a week reads the same
every time it is run.
"""
import csv
import hashlib
import html
import re
import sys
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

HARNESS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
INBOX = HARNESS / "inbox"
CACHE = HARNESS / "cache"
MAX_CHARS = 4000
WEEK_CHARS = 24000   # --week stays under this, so the shell shows it instead of saving it to a file


def _rows():
    for f in sorted(INBOX.glob("week-*.csv")):
        with open(f, newline="") as fh:
            for r in csv.DictReader(fh):
                r["week"] = int(f.stem.split("-")[1])
                yield r


def ids(week):
    """The link ids of one week, oldest first."""
    return [r["id"] for r in _rows() if r["week"] == int(week)]


def cache_path(url):
    return CACHE / (hashlib.sha1(url.encode()).hexdigest()[:16] + ".txt")


def _download(url):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (briefing-agent)"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=15) as resp:
        raw = resp.read(2_000_000).decode("utf-8", "replace")
    raw = re.sub(r"(?is)<(script|style|nav|footer|svg)\b.*?</\1>", " ", raw)
    text = html.unescape(re.sub(r"(?s)<[^>]+>", " ", raw))
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()


def get(link_id, limit=MAX_CHARS):
    """The text of one link: title, source, date, then the page."""
    row = next((r for r in _rows() if r["id"] == link_id), None)
    if row is None:
        return f"{link_id}: no such link in inbox/"
    path = cache_path(row["url"])
    if not path.exists():
        CACHE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        try:
            body = _download(row["url"])
        except Exception as e:  # a dead link is still a link the reader saved
            body = f"(could not fetch the page: {e})"
        path.write_text(body)
    head = f"{row['id']} | {row['date']} | {row['source']} | {row['title']}\n{row['url']}\n"
    page = path.read_text()
    return head + page[:limit] + (" [...]" if len(page) > limit else "")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        raise SystemExit(__doc__)
    week = sys.argv[1] == "--week" and len(sys.argv) > 2
    wanted = ids(sys.argv[2]) if week else sys.argv[1:]
    limit = min(MAX_CHARS, WEEK_CHARS // max(len(wanted), 1) - 150) if week else MAX_CHARS
    cut = False
    for link_id in wanted:
        text = get(link_id, limit)
        cut = cut or text.endswith(" [...]")
        print(text)
        print()
    if week and cut:
        print(f"(Pages marked [...] are cut to {limit} characters so the whole week fits on one "
              f"screen. For a whole page: python3 tools/fetch.py L001)")

# Memory

One-off corrections, one line each. A correction that keeps coming back belongs in CLAUDE.md, not here.

- News about a model itself (a new or domain-trained model, a lab's finding about how a model reasons or behaves, reactions to such a finding) is noise: the reader builds the harness around the model. It is signal only if the post hands them a concrete change to how they build, run or check an agent; "this might affect evals" is not enough. (R1)
- F3 does not cover a product launch (a hardware SDK, a design or art pack, an app) that only says "point your coding agent at the repo" or ships a skill for making more of that product. Ask: would this make the reader's agent better at building, running or checking any project? If it only helps make that one product, it is noise. (R2)

I added one line, tagged (R5), to `harness/memory.md`. Nothing has been run yet; the next round's scores will show whether it works.

- **The miss:** L061 was dropped in all 3 runs of week 3. When the agent fetched it, all it got was a three-line teaser about agents deciding what to fix and build, then "Attached: X article". The article itself was never available to read.
- **Why rounds 3 and 4 were reverted:** both told the agent to cite teasers like that. L061 came back each time, but the agent started citing posts because of what they quoted or attached:
  - L011 went from 1 of 3 runs to 3 of 3 in both rounds. It's a hype post about a launch video that attaches a harness-engineering article.
  - Round 3 also cited L044, a market forecast about another team's agent swarm.
  - Round 4's extra clause (skip posts that comment on another team's work) made it drop L039, a should-have link.
- **The new rule:** judge a post by its author's own words, not by the topic of what it quotes or attaches. Hype about something a model made is noise, even with a harness article attached. A forecast about a market is noise. Words that say how the author would have agents run, decide or check work are signal, even in a short teaser whose article can't be read.

REASON: Added a memory.md line (R5): judge a post by the author's own words, not by what it attaches; hype or market forecasts are noise even with a harness article attached, and the author's own plan for how agents run, decide or check work is signal even as a short teaser.
PREDICT: Fixes the week-3 miss L061 (3/3 runs) and lowers the week-1 noise L011 (1/3) without adding L044 as noise or losing L039.
